This PR started causing unit test failures on master

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f1f7a4d-f33c-4663-943a-66099d70c2de)

```
=== FAIL: k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache TestGenericListerListMethod (0.00s)
    listers_test.go:126: unexpected object has been returned expected = [0xc000a64050 0xc000a64058 0xc000a64060] actual = [0xc000a64048 0xc000a64038 0xc000a64040], diff =   []runtime.Object{
        + 	&unstructured.Unstructured{
        + 		Object: map[string]any{
        + 			"apiVersion": string("group/version"),
        + 			"kind":       string("TheKind"),
        + 			"metadata":   map[string]any{"name": string("name-bar"), "namespace": string("ns-bar")},
        + 		},
        + 	},
          	&unstructured.Unstructured{Object: {"apiVersion": string("group/version"), "kind": string("TheKind"), "metadata": map[string]any{"name": string("name-foo"), "namespace": string("ns-foo")}}},
          	&unstructured.Unstructured{Object: {"apiVersion": string("group/version"), "kind": string("TheKind"), "metadata": map[string]any{"name": string("name-foo1"), "namespace": string("ns-foo")}}},
        - 	&unstructured.Unstructured{
        - 		Object: map[string]any{
        - 			"apiVersion": string("group/version"),
        - 			"kind":       string("TheKind"),
        - 			"metadata":   map[string]any{"name": string("name-bar"), "namespace": string("ns-bar")},
        - 		},
        - 	},
          }
```
Guessing indexer uses map and doesn't guarantee order.

Options to just unblock master:
* Sort `actualOutput` before comparing. Don't know where to easily find a sort function for runtime.Object.
* use `assert.ElementsMatch` <- Go purist might not like it.
* Revert

Recommendation:
* indexer should sort before returning as the apiserver guarantees that results are sorted. Watchcache that uses indexer sorts results before returning. Don't know if we make it explicit API property since https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/metrics-server/pull/481

> Options:
> 
> * Sort `actualOutput` before comparing. Don't know where to easily find a sort function for runtime.Object.
> * use `assert.ElementsMatch` <- Go purist might not like it.
> * Revert

+1 to sort.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130745 should do it.  Apologies for missing this in  review.

review_comments: is the ListAll guaranteed to return the objects in the same order?

Yes, The sort order is lexographical by name.  Kube simply retains the order etcd provides from it's keyspace, so it's a defacto ordering that is backed into the API to the point where we would never change it.  We do depend on this order for things like [--limit](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/api-concepts/#retrieving-large-results-sets-in-chunks).

EDIT: But if your question @aojea is about the order specifically of the lister, I don't know that.  I'd hope it's the same as a kube list request, but I haven't verified that.
